purpose: Chemical-first, compound-specific exposure research. No CO2-derived toxicity ranks, no inferred company releases.

boundaries.climate: CO2 is used by plants in photosynthesis and is tracked under climate forcing; it is excluded from this direct chemical-toxicity and odor explorer. Elevated CO2 can pose occupational asphyxiation risks; this distinction is not a claim that climate effects are harmless.
boundaries.missing: Missing compound mass is unknown, never zero. No company hazard rank without like-for-like facility, year, speciation, receptor, and source evidence.
boundaries.rankings: Only rank masses within identical source/year/coverage/unit boundaries, not chemical toxicity. Odor is a qualitative sensory description, never a proxy for safety.
boundaries.exposure: Emission mass is not ambient concentration, absorbed dose, health outcome, injury compensation, or culpability. Pollutants formed in the atmosphere must not be double-counted as direct stack releases.

headline_sets.scope: US conventional power plants and combined-heat-and-power plants; energy-use emissions for electricity and useful thermal output
headline_sets.source_title: U.S. EIA Electric Power Annual 2025 · Table 9.1 (released Oct 21, 2026)
headline_sets.note: EIA estimates in metric tonnes; not a coal-only or company-specific inventory.

headline_sets.scope: US power plants subject to ARP, CSAPR and/or MATS reporting; EPA Power Plant Data Highlights
headline_sets.source_title: US EPA · Power Plant Data Highlights 2024 (February 2025)
headline_sets.note: Values are rounded as in EPA fact sheet. US short tons (2,000 lb) are not metric tonnes. This population differs from EIA 2025 coverage. NOₓ is a group total; Hg is mercury emissions, not methylmercury exposure.

compounds.name: Sulfur dioxide
compounds.coal_role: Coal and other sulfur-containing fuel combustion; also industrial smelting
compounds.chemistry: Gas-phase SO₂; oxidizes to sulfate aerosol and contributes to sulfuric acid deposition. Do not label every SO₂ ton as sulfuric acid.
compounds.health: Airway irritation and asthma exacerbation with short-term exposure; indirect fine-particle burden.
compounds.environment: Sulfate PM, acid deposition, sensitive lakes, forests and crops.
compounds.odor_note: Pungent irritating gas; odor alone is not an exposure metric.
compounds.measurement: National power-sector emissions are available, but not comparable to metal toxicity per ton.

sources.title: ATSDR · Sulfur trioxide and sulfuric acid

compounds.name: Nitrogen oxides (NO + NO₂)
compounds.coal_role: High-temperature combustion of coal and other fuels
compounds.chemistry: NOₓ is an aggregated reporting class dominated by nitric oxide and nitrogen dioxide—not a single chemical or NO₂ concentration.
compounds.health: NO₂ irritates airways and can aggravate asthma; NOₓ contributes to secondary PM₂.₅ and ozone.
compounds.environment: Nitrate particles, acid deposition and nitrogen enrichment.
compounds.odor_note: NO₂ can be acrid; the measured NOₓ mixture must not be presented as a single odorant.
compounds.measurement: Report aggregate NOₓ mass separately from ambient NO₂ and ozone concentrations.

compounds.name: Mercury (reported total)
compounds.coal_role: Trace constituent of coal; may escape stacks or partition into ash and controls
compounds.chemistry: Emitted elemental, oxidized and particle-bound species have different fates. Aquatic microbes can produce methylmercury; total Hg emissions are not methylmercury releases.
compounds.health: Species and route matter: methylmercury is a developmental neurotoxin; fish consumption is a key pathway.
compounds.environment: Deposition into water and food-web bioaccumulation.
compounds.odor_note: Mercury vapor is odorless; absence of smell does not imply absence of hazard.
compounds.measurement: EPA 2024 power data report total mercury emissions in short tons. No company-by-company total is imported.

sources.title: EPA · How People Are Exposed to Mercury

compounds.name: Arsenic and inorganic compounds
compounds.coal_role: Coal ash/particulates; ash-pond or groundwater pathways
compounds.chemistry: Elemental arsenic CAS is an identifier anchor, not a substitute for arsenite, arsenate or individual inorganic arsenic compounds.
compounds.health: Inorganic arsenic exposure can cause cancers and non-cancer effects; dose and speciation matter.
compounds.environment: Leaching from unmanaged ash into groundwater and waterways.
compounds.odor_note: Do not use smell to screen for arsenic.
compounds.measurement: No nationwide arsenic mass in this matched headline set. TRI/CCR facility measurements need explicit speciation.

compounds.name: Lead and compounds
compounds.coal_role: Trace metal in combustion residues and potentially particulate releases
compounds.chemistry: Total lead and lead compounds vary in solubility, particle size, and bioaccessibility; mass is not a blood-lead dose.
compounds.health: Neurodevelopmental risks, especially to children; no identified safe blood-lead level in children.
compounds.environment: Persistent contamination in soils and sediments.
compounds.odor_note: Lead contamination is generally not detected by smell.
compounds.measurement: Needs EPA TRI/CCR source records and medium-specific exposures.

compounds.name: Cadmium and compounds
compounds.coal_role: Trace coal-ash contaminant and potential airborne particulate constituent
compounds.chemistry: Element/compound form and leachability determine exposure; ash content is not a direct discharge.
compounds.health: Chronic cadmium exposure raises concern for kidney damage; some compounds are carcinogenic.
compounds.environment: Contamination of sediment, soil and water from releases.
compounds.odor_note: Do not rely on odor as a signal.
compounds.measurement: No verified matched nationwide annual mass in this dataset.

compounds.name: Hexavalent chromium compounds
compounds.coal_role: Some coal/industrial metal emissions; measured chromium must be speciated before calling it Cr(VI)
compounds.chemistry: Chromium(VI) and chromium(III) are chemically and toxicologically distinct. Total chromium release cannot be relabeled as Cr(VI).
compounds.health: Specific hexavalent compounds can cause cancer and respiratory damage through relevant exposures.
compounds.environment: Mobility depends on oxidation state and water chemistry.
compounds.odor_note: Chromium species are not reliably detectable by smell.
compounds.measurement: Require Cr(VI)-specific measurements; no automatic conversions from total Cr.

sources.title: EPA · Hazardous air pollutants from power plants

compounds.name: Selenium compounds
compounds.coal_role: Coal-combustion wastewater and ash leachate may contain selenium
compounds.chemistry: Essential trace nutrient at low intake, toxic at elevated exposure; species including selenate/selenite differ.
compounds.health: Exposure context is essential; not all selenium presence is poisoning.
compounds.environment: May bioaccumulate and cause fish and bird reproductive effects in affected ecosystems.
compounds.odor_note: Dissolved selenium is not detected by smell.
compounds.measurement: Requires effluent concentrations, species, receiving waters and ecological context.

compounds.name: Sulfuric acid aerosol / mist
compounds.coal_role: Can be generated from SO₃ and oxidation of SO₂; some industrial processes emit acid mist directly
compounds.chemistry: Sulfuric acid aerosol is not equivalent to emitted SO₂ mass; avoid summing derived sulfate with precursor SO₂ without atmospheric modeling.
compounds.health: Acid mist can irritate and injure respiratory tissue; route and particle size matter.
compounds.odor_note: Acid mist irritation does not provide a quantitative odor exposure measure.
compounds.measurement: Need actual mist sampling or defensible secondary aerosol model.

compounds.name: Fine particulate matter
compounds.coal_role: Direct fly ash and secondary sulfate/nitrate aerosol from SO₂ and NOₓ
compounds.chemistry: Size class ≤2.5 μm, NOT a specific chemical formula; composition, metal content, dose and source vary.
compounds.health: Associated with cardiovascular and respiratory disease; fine particles penetrate lungs.
compounds.environment: Haze and deposition; mixtures can contain acidic or metallic species.
compounds.odor_note: Particles do not have a universal odor; smoke smell is not a particle-mass measurement.
compounds.measurement: Use ambient μg/m³ or direct stack emissions under specified boundaries; do not present as a single compound.

sources.title: EPA · PM Health and Environmental Effects

compounds.name: Hydrogen chloride / hydrochloric acid gas
compounds.coal_role: Acid gas in coal-fired electric generation and certain industrial combustion
compounds.chemistry: Gas dissolves readily in water to form acidic solution; distinguish emissions from hydrochloric acid liquid handling.
compounds.health: Strong respiratory irritant at sufficient concentrations.
compounds.environment: Acidic deposition and local damage depending on concentration.
compounds.odor_note: Pungent odor possible, but not a substitute for monitoring.
compounds.measurement: EPA MATS regulates acid gas hazards; no headline mass here.

compounds.name: Hydrogen fluoride / hydrofluoric acid
compounds.coal_role: A hazardous acid-gas constituent of some coal and industrial combustion streams
compounds.chemistry: Gas vs aqueous acid differs; fluoride dose, speciation and exposure route matter.
compounds.health: Can injure airways and tissues with sufficient exposure; severe occupational releases pose distinct risk.
compounds.environment: Local plant and ecosystem injury can depend on deposited fluoride.
compounds.odor_note: Do not assume safe air from an absent odor.
compounds.measurement: Requires acid-gas monitoring; no compatible annual figure in this selection.

compounds.name: Hydrogen sulfide
compounds.coal_role: Important in sour gas, refineries, mines and industrial operations; not automatically a coal stack emission
compounds.chemistry: Reduced sulfur gas, chemically distinct from SO₂ and sulfuric acid.
compounds.health: High concentrations may rapidly cause collapse, poisoning or death; odor fatigue makes smell unsafe for warning.
compounds.environment: Can affect air quality near industrial and waste sources.
compounds.odor_note: Strong rotten-egg smell at low concentrations, but olfactory fatigue/paralysis can remove warning at dangerous levels.
compounds.measurement: No emissions value assigned to coal firms without facility-level reporting.

sources.title: OSHA · H₂S hazards and smell warning

compounds.name: Formaldehyde
compounds.coal_role: An organic hazardous air pollutant in some combustion and industrial operations; not a unique coal signature
compounds.chemistry: Reactive aldehyde; gas-phase ambient chemistry and direct releases need differentiated sources.
compounds.health: Irritation and carcinogenic concerns in relevant chronic inhalation exposures.
compounds.environment: Reacts in the atmosphere; exposure context matters.
compounds.odor_note: Distinct odor possible but it is not a reliable concentration measure.
compounds.measurement: No national matched value imported in this selection.
